blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Distribution matching distillation (DMD) has emerged as a leading paradigm for distilling diffusion models into few-step students, where an auxiliary fake score model tracks the student's distribution and the discrepancy between the teacher and fake predictions drives the student toward the teacher. In multi-step distillation, although only the student's final output is delivered, existing methods train the fake model on intermediate states or across all denoising steps. Consequently, the student's update signal becomes entangled with intermediate distributions, which can distort the matching direction and remain nonzero even after the student's final outputs already match the teacher distribution. To resolve this mismatch, we propose Endpoint Distribution Matching Distillation (eDMD), which trains a single shared fake model exclusively on the student's final outputs and uses it to correct every denoising step. Our theoretical analysis proves that this endpoint reference guarantees that the distribution matching term vanishes if and only if the student's final output distribution matches the teacher's, regardless of intermediate distributions. Beyond the fake reference, we further strengthen teacher supervision through a precise teacher (PT) that replaces single-step guided predictions with short multi-step trajectories on the final noise interval, paired with a calibrated query density for intermediate steps. Experiments on SD3-Medium, FLUX.2-klein (4B and 9B), and Qwen-Image-2.1 demonstrate that eDMD consistently outperforms existing distribution matching methods for 4-step generation.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Diffusion and flow matching models have achieved remarkable success in high-quality image [ 10 , 6 ] , video [ 50 ] , and audio [ 22 ] generation.
However, their iterative sampling processes typically require tens of network evaluations, resulting in substantial inference costs.
Few-step distillation addresses this limitation by transferring the generative capabilities of a pretrained teacher into a student that requires only one or a few denoising steps [ 44 , 49 , 40 , 19 ] .
Among existing approaches, distribution matching distillation (DMD) has emerged as one of the most effective and widely adopted paradigms [ 33 , 62 ] .
While DMD has demonstrated impressive one-step generation capabilities, a single network evaluation often struggles to preserve fine-grained details and complex structures [ 61 ] .
Recent methods therefore extend DMD to multi-step generation, allowing the student to progressively refine its predictions and achieve higher generation quality while maintaining efficient inference [ 61 , 34 , 21 , 23 ] .
blocks.zh:
传播和流相匹配模型在高质量图像[10,6],视频[50],音频[22]生成方面都取得了显著成功.
然而,它们的迭代取样过程通常需要数十次网络评价,从而产生大量推论费用。
很少分级分级分级解决了这种局限性,将经过预先训练的教师的分级能力转移到只需要一个或几个去命名步骤的学生身上[44,49,40,19].
在现有的方法中,分布相匹配蒸馏法(DMD)已成为最为有效并被广泛采纳的范式之一[33,62].
虽然DMD展现出令人印象深刻的一步生成能力,但单一的网络评价往往难以保存精细的细节和复杂结构 [61].
因此,最近的方法将DMD扩展至多步骤生成,使学生能够逐步完善预测并实现更高的生成质量,同时保持高效的推论[61,34,21,23].

blocks.en:
The central idea of DMD is to train the student by minimizing the distributional discrepancy between its generated samples and those of the pretrained teacher.
Specifically, DMD formulates this objective through the reverse Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence between their noise-perturbed distributions, whose gradient can be estimated from the difference between the teacher’s and student’s score functions [ 62 ] .
Since the student’s score is not directly available, DMD introduces an auxiliary diffusion model, known as the fake score model , which is trained online on student-generated samples to approximate the student’s distribution.
The discrepancy between the teacher’s prediction, often enhanced with classifier-free guidance (CFG) [ 9 ] , and the fake model’s estimate then provides the correction signal for updating the student.
Importantly, the distribution learned by the fake model determines the reference against which the student is optimized.
When denoising is performed in a single step, the student’s prediction is also its final generated output, making the distribution learned by the fake model naturally consistent with the desired matching objective.
When denoising involves multiple steps, however, the student produces a sequence of intermediate predictions before generating its final output.
These predictions generally follow different distributions, so how the fake model is trained becomes a central design choice.
blocks.zh:
DMD的中心思想是培训学生,尽量缩小其生成的样本与被预先培训的教师样本之间的分布差距.
具体地说,DMD通过反向的Kullback - Leibler(KL)在噪声扰动的分布上的差异来制定这一目标,其梯度可以从师生分数函数的相差来估计[62].
由于学生的分数无法直接获得,DMD引入了一个辅助传播模型,称为"假分数模型",该模型在网上接受学生所生成样本的培训,以大致了解学生的分数.
教师的预测(通常用无分级制导(CFG)[9]来强化)与假模型的估计之间的相差,然后为学生更新提供了校正信号.
重要的是,由假模型所学到的分布决定了学生最优化的参考.
当逐个步骤地进行去名化时,学生的预测也是其最终产生的输出,使假模型所学出的分配自然符合所期望的匹配目标.
然而,当取名涉及多个步骤时,学生在生成其最终产出之前会生成一系列中间预测.
这些预测一般遵循不同的分布,因此假模型如何被训练成为中央设计选择.

blocks.en:
Existing multi-step DMD methods incorporate intermediate predictions or states into the training of the fake model ( Fig. 2 ), following two paradigms.
The first, represented by DMD2 [ 61 ] , trains a shared fake model using predictions collected from different denoising steps, effectively learning a mixture of intermediate and final prediction distributions.
The second, represented by TDM [ 34 ] , constructs stage-dependent references from intermediate denoising states and performs distribution matching within their corresponding noise intervals.
Despite their different implementations, both paradigms couple the distribution matching objective to intermediate distributions, whereas the ultimate goal of distillation is to match the student’s final output distribution to the teacher’s.
This distinction is particularly important for few-step students, which compress a complex generative process into only a few steps.
Their intermediate predictions need not follow the teacher’s corresponding distributions, even when their final outputs accurately reproduce the teacher’s distribution.
Therefore, imposing distributional constraints on intermediate predictions may introduce unnecessary restrictions and interfere with the optimization of final generation quality.
blocks.zh:
现有的多步骤DMD方法将中间预测或状态纳入假模型(图2)的训练中,遵循了两个范式.
第一种以DMD2 [61]为代表,利用从不同去名步骤所收集的预测,训练出一个共享的假模型,有效地学习了中间和最终预测分布的混合.
第二套由TDM[34]所代表,从中间去诺状态构造相依赖的相位参考,并在相应的噪声间隔内进行相配.
尽管两者的执行不同,但两种范式都把分配目标与中间分配相匹配,而蒸馏的最终目标是将学生的最终产出分配与教师的分布相匹配。
这种区分对于几个步骤的学生来说特别重要,这把复杂的基因过程压缩成只有几个步骤.
他们的中间预测不需要遵循教师的相应分布,即使他们的最终产出准确地复制了教师的分布.
因此,对中间预测施加分布限制可能会引入不必要的限制并干扰最终生成质量的优化.

blocks.en:
To understand the consequences of this mismatch, we theoretically analyze how the fake model’s reference distribution influences the student update.
We denote the distribution of the student’s final outputs as the endpoint distribution .
Under exact conditional denoisers, we decompose the DMD correction signal into three components ( Eq. 3 ): a teacher enhancement term arising from guidance, an endpoint matching term that measures the discrepancy between the teacher and the student’s final output distribution, and an additional reference residual caused by the discrepancy between the fake model’s reference distribution and the endpoint distribution.
Our analysis reveals that existing intermediate-based references can introduce a nonzero residual that fundamentally changes the intended distribution matching behavior.
Even when the student’s final output distribution already matches the teacher’s, this residual may remain nonzero and continue to push the student away from the desired distribution.
We further prove that the reference residual vanishes if and only if the fake model represents the endpoint distribution, regardless of the student’s intermediate distributions ( Prop. 1 ).
Our two-dimensional synthetic experiments confirm these effects, showing that intermediate-based references deflect the update from the desired direction, whereas an endpoint-aligned reference does not ( Fig. 3 ).
blocks.zh:
我们从理论上分析假模型的参考分布如何影响学生更新。
我们表示学生最后产出的分配是终点的分配。
在精确的有条件的Demoisers下,我们把DMD校正信号分解成三个部分(Eq. 3):一个由向导产生的教师增强名词,一个测量老师和学生最终产出分配的端点匹配名词,以及由假模型的参考分布和端点分布相差而来的额外参考剩余.
我们的分析显示,现有的基于中间的引用可以引入一种非零的残余,从根本上改变预期的分布匹配行为.
即使学生的最终产出分配已经与教师相符,这一剩余部分可能仍为非零,并继续将学生推向预期的分配。
我们进一步证明,如果并且只有在假模型代表终点分布时,不管学生中间分布(Propos. 1),参考残留就会消失。
我们的二维合成实验证实了这些效果,显示中间基参考物使更新偏离了所期望的方向,而端点相通的参考物则没有(图3)。

blocks.en:
These findings motivate a simple principle: the fake model should represent the distribution of the samples that distillation ultimately aims to optimize, rather than the intermediate predictions used to generate them.
Based on this principle, we propose Endpoint Distribution Matching Distillation ( eDMD ), which trains a single shared fake model exclusively on the student’s final generated outputs and uses it to provide correction signals for every denoising step.
By aligning the fake model’s reference with the endpoint distribution, eDMD eliminates the reference residual and ensures that the distribution matching signal is determined by the discrepancy between the teacher and the student’s final outputs, independently of the intermediate sampling trajectory ( Corollary 1 ).
This allows intermediate steps to take whatever form best suits few-step generation, without imposing unnecessary distributional constraints.
blocks.zh:
这些发现激励了一个简单的原则:假模型应代表最终旨在优化蒸馏的样品的分布,而不是用来生成这些样品的中间预测.
基于这个原则,我们提出 Endpoint 分布匹配分化(eDMD),它专门根据学生最终产生的输出来训练一个共享的假模型,并利用它为每一个去诺步骤提供校正信号.
eDMD通过将假模型的参考值与端点分布相匹配,消除了参考值后遗症,并确保分配匹配信号由老师和学生最终产出的差异决定,独立于中间采样轨迹(Corollary 1 ).
这使得中间步骤可以采取任何最合适的形式,几步生成,而不会施加不必要的分配限制。

blocks.en:
Beyond correcting the student-side distribution reference, effective DMD also depends on the quality of the supervision provided by the teacher.
D-DMD [ 21 ] identifies CFG augmentation of the teacher prediction as the primary engine of few-step distillation.
However, existing methods typically obtain teacher targets through a single guided network evaluation at each sampled noise level.
Such predictions can average over multiple plausible outputs and lose fine-grained details, whereas the teacher achieves high-quality generation through iterative denoising ( Fig. 2 , bottom).
To improve the precision of teacher supervision, we introduce a precise teacher (PT) that replaces single-step teacher predictions with short multi-step guided trajectories within the final denoising interval, providing sharper and more accurate supervision without increasing student inference cost.
Furthermore, teacher predictions are not equally reliable across noise levels, as guidance and model approximation errors can introduce inconsistencies between predictions at different noise levels.
Uniformly sampling noise levels may therefore expose intermediate student steps to unreliable supervision.
To address this issue, we introduce a calibrated query density that estimates the teacher’s cross-level prediction consistency before distillation and concentrates intermediate-step queries on noise levels that provide more reliable supervision.
blocks.zh:
有效的DMD除了纠正学生-侧分配参考之外,还取决于教师提供的监管质量.
D-DMD [21]确定CFG增强教师预测是几步蒸馏的主要引擎.
然而,现有方法通常通过对每个取样噪音水平的单一指导网络评价获得教师目标。
这种预测可以平均超过多种可能的产出,并失去精细的细节,而教师则通过迭代代名(图2,下方)实现高质量的代代.
为了提高教师监管的精度,我们引入了一个精确的教师(PT),在最终去名间隔内用短多步制导轨取而代之的单步教师预测,在不增加学生推导成本的情况下提供更尖锐更准确的监管.
此外,教师的预测在噪声级别上并不同样可靠,因为制导和模型近似误差可以造成不同噪声级别上预测之间的不一致.
因此,统一取样的噪音水平可能使中学生的步骤受到不可靠的监督。
为了解决这个问题,我们引入了一个校正的查询密度,该密度在分馏前估计老师的跨层次预测一致性,并将中间步骤的查询集中在噪音水平上,从而提供更可靠的监督.

blocks.en:
Overall, eDMD aligns the distribution matching objective with the student’s final outputs and improves the quality of teacher supervision.
We evaluate eDMD on four representative diffusion and flow matching backbones (SD3-Medium [ 6 ] , FLUX.2-klein-4B, FLUX.2-klein-9B [ 2 ] , and Qwen-Image-2.1 [ 38 ] ), distilling each into a 4-step generator without using real images.
Extensive experiments demonstrate that eDMD consistently outperforms existing distribution matching baselines, achieving the highest peak HPSv3++ [ 26 ] scores across all four backbones.
Our main contributions are summarized as follows: • We identify and theoretically characterize an objective mismatch in multi-step DMD: training the fake model on intermediate predictions introduces a reference residual that distorts distribution matching and vanishes if and only if the fake model learns the endpoint distribution. • We propose eDMD , which trains a shared fake model exclusively on the student’s final outputs and strengthens teacher supervision through a multi-step precise teacher (PT) and a calibrated query density. • Experiments on four backbones show consistent improvements over existing distribution matching methods, with higher human-preference scores, improved fine-grained details, and fewer structural artifacts.
blocks.zh:
总的来说,eDMD使分配目标与学生的最终产出相匹配,并提高了教师监督的质量.
我们评价了4个具有代表性的传播和流相匹配主干线(SD3-Medium [6],FLUX.2-克林-4B,FLUX.2-克林-9B [2],和Qun-Image-2.1 [38]),在不使用真实图像的情况下将每个主干线蒸馏成4步生成器.
广泛的实验表明,eDMD一贯优于现有分布匹配基线,在所有四个主干线上都实现了最高峰值HPSv3++ [26]分.
我们的主要贡献概述如下: 我们在多步骤DMD中识别并理论上定性一个客观的不匹配:在中间预测上培训假模型引入了一种参考后遗症,该参考后遗症扭曲了分布匹配,并只在假模型学会了端点分布的情况下消失. ^ 我们提议eDMD, 专门根据学生的最终产出来训练一个共享的假模型, · 4个主干线的试验显示,与现有的分配比对方法相比,持续改进,人类偏好分数较高,精细细细细细,结构文物较少.

blocks.en: 2 Related work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Few-step diffusion distillation. Few-step distillation trains a student to match the quality of a diffusion or flow matching teacher [ 10 , 48 , 20 ] in only a few sampling steps.
Trajectory-based methods train the student to follow the teacher’s sampling path: progressive distillation merges adjacent steps [ 44 , 36 ] , rectified flows straighten the path [ 24 , 25 ] , and consistency and flow-map methods learn direct mappings from noisy states to cleaner states [ 49 , 32 , 15 , 52 , 40 , 29 , 41 ] .
Adversarial methods instead align output distributions using a discriminator against real or teacher samples [ 46 , 45 , 19 ] .
Distribution matching, which our work builds upon, aligns them using score estimates from the teacher and an online fake model.

blocks.en:
Distribution matching distillation. Building on score distillation for text-to-3D generation [ 37 , 55 ] , Diff-Instruct and DMD update the student with the score difference between the pretrained teacher and a fake model trained online on the student’s samples [ 33 , 62 ] .
Subsequent work explores alternative divergences [ 65 , 60 , 54 ] , incorporates adversarial objectives [ 61 , 31 ] , refines the fake score estimate or the update direction [ 7 , 58 ] , or mitigates mode collapse [ 56 , 18 ] .
DMD2 extends DMD to multi-step generation [ 61 ] , a setting adopted by many later methods [ 21 , 23 , 34 , 66 , 27 , 56 ] .
Their fake models are typically trained on intermediate predictions or states, whereas we show that only a fake model trained on final outputs avoids biasing the student update.
This also explains a choice found in some implementations: ADM fits its fake model to final outputs in its training algorithm [ 31 ] , and the final-step matching variant of SiD supervises only the final output by back-propagating through the entire sampling chain [ 66 ] , whereas eDMD corrects every step directly.

blocks.en:
Teacher supervision. Distillation relies on the quality of the teacher’s supervision.
For diffusion models, generation quality often depends on guidance, from CFG [ 9 ] and its refinements [ 17 , 53 , 42 ] to guidance by a weaker model [ 14 ] or by perturbed attention [ 1 ] .
D-DMD shows that the same holds in DMD: CFG augmentation of the teacher prediction is the primary engine of few-step distillation, with distribution matching acting as a regularizer [ 21 ] .
Strengthening the teacher’s supervision is therefore a direct way to improve the student, for example by fine-tuning the teacher [ 34 ] , targeting a reward-tilted teacher distribution [ 13 ] , or deriving regression targets from the teacher’s own denoising outputs [ 68 , 46 , 8 , 56 ] .
blocks.zh:
师监督. 蒸发取决于教师监督的质量。
对于传播模型,生成质量往往取决于指导,从CFG[9]及其改进[17,53,42]到较弱的模型[14]或受扰的注意[1]。
D-DMD显示在DMD中同样存在: CFG增强教师预测是几步蒸馏的主要引擎,分布相配起到调节器的作用 [21].
因此,加强教师的监督是改善学生状况的直接途径,例如通过微调教师[34],针对奖励教师分配[13],或从教师自己虚名的产出中得出回归目标[68、46、8、56]。

blocks.en:
Following Alg. 1 , we perform five fake updates (each with fresh prompts and a detached rollout) per student update, which reuses the final rollout and backpropagates only through the selected step.
Query calibration is performed once per teacher and grid before training; sampling from the precomputed densities adds no teacher evaluations during distillation.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
We showed that training the fake model on intermediate predictions or states can distort distribution matching in multi-step DMD.
The resulting reference residual can persist even after the student’s final output distribution matches the teacher’s. eDMD resolves this mismatch with an endpoint reference, training a shared fake model exclusively on final outputs and using it to supervise every denoising step.
This keeps distribution matching focused on the samples delivered at inference and gives intermediate predictions the freedom to adapt to few-step generation.
We further improve teacher supervision in two ways: a precise teacher (PT) refines low-noise targets through multi-step denoising, and a calibrated query density favors noise levels where teacher predictions are more reliable.
Experiments on four diffusion and flow matching backbones show that eDMD improves 4-step generation quality over existing distribution matching methods.
blocks.zh:
我们显示,在中间预测或状态上训练假模型,可以在多步骤的DMD中扭曲分布匹配.
即使学生的最终产出分配与教师的匹配,由此产生的参考残留仍可能继续存在。 eDMD通过一个端点参考解决了这种不匹配,专门在最终产出上培训一个共享的假模型,并利用它来监督每一个去名步骤.
这保持了分布匹配,侧重于推论中交付的样品,并给予中间预测以适应几步生成的自由.
我们以两种方式进一步改善教师监督:精确的教师(PT)通过多步骤去诺来完善低噪声目标,以及校正的查询密度有利于教师预测更可靠的噪音水平.

Local implementations and tuning. All locally trained baselines share our teacher-default guidance, batch size 16, rank-32 LoRA parameterization, and evaluation pipeline.
DMD2 uses its distribution matching and backward simulation objectives (without the GAN loss) and five fake updates per student update; we lowered the SDXL LoRA student learning rate from 5 × 10 − 5 5\times 10^{-5} (which oscillated after 200–400 updates) to 2 × 10 − 5 2\times 10^{-5} with fake rate 5 × 10 − 5 5\times 10^{-5} on FLUX.2-klein-4B and SD3-Medium.
D-DMD is reproduced from its paper and the implementation released with CDM [ 23 ] ; starting from CDM’s rates ( 10 − 5 10^{-5} / 5 × 10 − 6 5\times 10^{-6} ), we swept the student rate ( 5 × 10 − 6 5\times 10^{-6} ), fake rate ( 2 × 10 − 5 2\times 10^{-5} ), normalizer floor (0.01), and CA weight (0.5), retaining 5 × 10 − 6 5\times 10^{-6} for both networks on FLUX.2-klein-4B and SD3-Medium.
For CDM on FLUX.2-klein-4B, we swept LoRA student rates in [ 10 − 6 , 10 − 5 ] [10^{-6},10^{-5}] (constant and cosine), fake rates in [ 5 × 10 − 7 , 5 × 10 − 5 ] [5\times 10^{-7},5\times 10^{-5}] , and CA weights in { 0.5 , 1 } \{0.5,1\} , as well as batch-scaled full-parameter runs (which peaked at 8.96); Tab. 1 reports the best configuration (LoRA student 10 − 6 10^{-6} , fake 5 × 10 − 7 5\times 10^{-7} , CA weight 0.5).
For TDM on FLUX.2-klein-4B (student 4 × 10 − 6 4\times 10^{-6} , fake 2 × 10 − 5 2\times 10^{-5} ), our ℓ 2 \ell_{2} re-implementation—which incorporates the DMD normalizer into an ℓ 2 \ell_{2} surrogate target, samples intervals in σ \sigma , and uses five fake updates per student update—outperforms TDM’s official recipe (Huber loss divided by the normalizer and one fake update per student update; Tab. A.4 ).
On FLUX.2-klein-9B, student and fake learning rates are 10 − 6 10^{-6} and 2.5 × 10 − 5 2.5\times 10^{-5} for DMD2, 6.25 × 10 − 7 6.25\times 10^{-7} and 2.5 × 10 − 6 2.5\times 10^{-6} for D-DMD, 2 × 10 − 6 2\times 10^{-6} and 10 − 5 10^{-5} for TDM, and 5 × 10 − 7 5\times 10^{-7} and 2.5 × 10 − 7 2.5\times 10^{-7} for CDM; the official 4-step checkpoint uses its own pipeline at w = 1 w=1 .

blocks.en: Held-out selection. Because peak checkpoints in Tabs. 1 and 2 are selected and evaluated on the same 200 prompts, we assess selection bias across 1,000 random 100/100 prompt splits (keeping each prompt’s five seeds together), selecting each trained row’s checkpoint on one half and scoring it on the held-out half. eDMD ranks first on the held-out half in all 1,000 splits across all four teachers, leading the strongest baseline by 0.30, 1.37, 1.11, and 0.47 HPSv3++ on SD3-Medium, FLUX.2-klein-4B, FLUX.2-klein-9B, and Qwen-Image; across all rows, full-set selection exceeds held-out selection by at most 0.06 on average.
